analysis.title: Walt Disney Co. (DIS) F4Q26 preview: Reiterating our above-consensus F4Q26 estimates; updating quarterly cadence for F2027
key_insights: GS forecasts F4Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.73 vs Visible Alpha consensus of $1.66, segment EBIT (non-GAAP) of $4.93bn vs consensus $4.85bn (company guidance $4.9bn), and revenue of $25.43bn vs consensus $25.14bn.
The 53rd week in F4Q26 is expected to add about $600mn to total segment operating income and lift total revenues by an estimated 1.5% to 2.0%.
GS keeps its Buy rating and cuts the 12-month price target to $140 from $144 on slightly lower EBITDA. Price was $106.15, implying 31.9% upside.

F2027 adjusted EPS is $7.56 (+8% y/y reported, implied +12% underlying excluding the 53rd week headwind), raised slightly from $7.49 on a lower tax rate. Segment EBIT of $20.6bn is largely unchanged. Quarterly cadence was updated for calendar timing, content and product timing, Disney+ content investment and theme park capex.
GS estimates a 13% EPS CAGR for F2025-F2028E and calls Disney a multi-year earnings compounder in the early stages of a broader product and Experiences investment cycle.

Experiences F4Q26 revenue is forecast at $10.06bn (+15% y/y) vs consensus $9.87bn, and EBIT at $2.28bn (+21% y/y) vs consensus $2.24bn. Drivers are the Disney Destiny and Disney Adventure launches (stateroom capacity up about 50% y/y), domestic park price increases, stable domestic attendance and new attractions. Softer Asian park attendance and a Disney Wonder dry dock partly offset.
Domestic park attendance is modeled at +9% y/y reported and +1.5% underlying (vs +3% in F3Q26A), with per caps up 3% y/y. International attendance pressure at domestic parks moderated vs F2Q26.

Entertainment F4Q26 EBIT is forecast at $1.26bn (in line with consensus $1.26bn) on revenue of $11.50bn (vs $11.46bn). Offsets are weak Moana live-action box office, cord-cutting and a soft domestic SVOD ad market.

SVOD F4Q26 EBIT is forecast at $690mn (vs consensus $680mn) on revenue of $6.01bn (vs $5.86bn), implying 11.2% margins for F2026. Drivers are the pay-1 window for The Devil Wears Prada 2, The Mandalorian and Grogu and Toy Story 5, password-sharing crackdowns and price increases.

US Disney+ and Hulu prices rose effective September 23, 2026. Standalone premium plans rose $2.50 to $21.49, ad tiers rose $0.50 to $12.49 and the premium bundle rose $2.00 to $21.99. The increase came earlier than the usual October timing, and GS says the wider spread pushes users toward bundles.

Sports F4Q26 EBIT is forecast at $1.38bn (+52% y/y) vs consensus $1.35bn on revenue of $4.48bn vs $4.41bn. Drivers are expanded NFL rights, the WWE Premium Live Events deal, ESPN bundling and the absence of UFC rights amortization.

GS consolidated F2026/27/28 segment EBIT estimates are down 1% on average, with lower Entertainment and Experiences income partly offset by higher Sports. F2028 segment EBIT was cut 2% to $22,291mn and F2028 EPS to $8.61 from $8.69.
SVOD operating income estimates were cut for F2027 to $3,047mn (-11%) and for F2028 to $3,444mn (-18%). Sports OI for F2027 was raised 20% to $3,198mn.

Disney is executing a $60bn 10-year capex plan for Experiences (F2023-33) and targets a 13-vessel cruise fleet by the end of 2030. F2027 capex was raised 6% and F2028 capex 12%, which pulls down FCF estimates (F2028 FCF -8%).

Disney+ will add merchandise and interactive features in Spring 2027, plus a new FAST channel and a TikTok partnership, as churn-reduction tools. Disney plans to roughly triple its local original series over three years.
Avengers: Doomsday secured $50mn in pre-sales three months before its December release. The 2027-28 film slate includes Frozen 3, Incredibles 3 and The Bluey Movie.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated with the price target cut to $140 from $144 on slightly lower EBITDA. GS sees above-consensus F4Q26 estimates and a 13% EPS CAGR for F2025-F2028E.

sector_views.rationale: GS is constructive on Disney as a multi-year earnings compounder. Experiences and Sports growth and the content pipeline offset SVOD ad softness, cord-cutting and softer Asian park attendance.

earnings_insights: DIS F4Q26 adjusted diluted EPS estimate $1.73 (GS estimate, not yet reported) vs Visible Alpha consensus $1.66, up 56% y/y. Diluted GAAP EPS estimate $1.58 vs consensus $1.49.
DIS F4Q26 segment operating income (non-GAAP) estimate $4,927mn vs consensus $4,849mn and company guidance of about $4.9bn (estimates, not yet reported).
DIS F4Q26 revenue estimate $25,432mn (+13% y/y) vs consensus $25,135mn. The prior GS estimate was $25,711mn.

DIS F4Q26 segment estimates (GS vs consensus): Experiences revenue $10.06bn vs $9.87bn and EBIT $2.28bn vs $2.24bn. Entertainment revenue $11.50bn vs $11.46bn and EBIT $1.26bn vs $1.26bn. Sports revenue $4.48bn vs $4.41bn and EBIT $1.38bn vs $1.35bn.
DIS F4Q26 FCF estimate $3,897mn vs consensus $4,562mn, and capex estimate $2,232mn vs consensus $2,141mn.
DIS F2026E adjusted EPS $7.03 (unchanged, GS estimate), F2027E $7.56 (from $7.49) and F2028E $8.61 (from $8.69). F3Q26 adjusted EPS was $2.08 (reported).
The F4Q26 tax rate is estimated at 25.0%. F2027 tax rate was lowered to 23.5% from 25.0%, which adds about $259mn to F2027 net income.

F2026 segment guidance as cited by GS: Experiences high end of high-single-digit growth ex 53rd week, Entertainment double-digit growth ex 53rd week, Sports mid-single-digit growth ex 53rd week. GS estimates +12%, +15% and +7% respectively.
risk_factors: Higher than expected interest rates and FX moves.
Softer SVOD advertising, weaker Asian theme park attendance and Disney Wonder and Disney Wish dry docks (May 8-22, 2027 reportedly scheduled for the Wish).

tension_points.bull_case: Experiences growth from new cruise ships and park pricing, Sports growth from NFL and WWE rights, a strong film slate and Disney+ bundling support a 13% EPS CAGR and above-consensus F4Q26 estimates.
tension_points.bear_case: SVOD advertising softness, cord-cutting, softer Asian park attendance, weak Moana live-action box office and rising capex (F2028 FCF estimate cut 8%) are near-term headwinds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS cites key downside risks of intensified cord-cutting, sports rights cost inflation, streaming competition and weak consumer spending, but names no specific level or print.

theme_stances.key_argument: Disney is in the early stages of a broader product and Experiences investment cycle, including cruise fleet expansion and theme park capital investments.
GS reiterates above-consensus F4Q26 estimates, with segment EBIT largely unchanged.
